A content delivery network, or CDN, is a system of computers spread across many cities and countries that work together to deliver websites, videos, and other online content faster. Without one, every request for a webpage would travel all the way to a single origin server — the original computer where the website's files are permanently stored — no matter how far away the visitor happens to be. That long trip takes time, and the more distance involved, the slower a page feels.

A CDN solves this by placing copies of that content on many computers positioned closer to where people actually are. Each of these nearby computers is called an edge location, because it sits at the edge of the network, near the audience rather than near the origin server. When someone visits a website, the request is automatically routed to the nearest edge location instead of the distant origin server. If that edge location already has a saved copy of the requested content, the result is called a cache hit, meaning the answer was found nearby and delivered almost instantly, without contacting the origin server at all. Think of it like a chain of neighborhood libraries that each keep copies of popular books, so readers never have to travel to one faraway central library every time. When a cache hit does not happen, the edge location fetches the content from the origin server once and stores a copy for next time, so future visitors benefit from the shorter trip. The overall effect is a web that feels quicker and more reliable for people everywhere, regardless of location.

| Term | Plain meaning | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Origin server | The original computer storing a website's real files | It is the ultimate source all copies come from |
| Edge location | A nearby computer holding copies of content | It shortens the distance content must travel |
| Cache hit | A request answered from a nearby saved copy | It means faster delivery and less strain on the origin |
| Content delivery network | The whole network of edge locations working together | It keeps online experiences fast worldwide |
